title: The Same Code, Two Worlds: A Plant Interface and the Contract a Fake Must Keep

questions.question: Why must a controller not know whether it is talking to a simulation or hardware?
options: Because hardware is too slow to be told apart from a simulation
So that nothing in it changes between the two, and what passed in simulation is what runs on the machine
So that the simulation can be made faster than the hardware
Because the controller has no way to ask
questions.explanation: If the controller is the same code on both sides of the interface, then what was tested in simulation is exactly what is put on the machine.

questions.question: A first order motor of time constant 0.1 s is given a step command. How far has its speed got after 0.1 s?
options: 50 percent: 3.000 of 6.0, and 100 percent after two time constants
100 percent: a time constant is the time to reach the final speed
10 percent: 0.600 of 6.0, and 63 percent after five time constants
About 63 percent: 3.804 of 6.0, and 99 percent after five time constants
questions.explanation: A first order response covers 63 percent of the way in one time constant, here 3.804 of 6.0, and 5.961 after five.

questions.question: What does the saturation rule check?
options: That the plant never reaches its limit in normal use
That the limit is the same in both directions
That a command ten times the limit does exactly what the limit does: a plant with no clamp broke it
That a command at the limit gives twice what half the limit gives
questions.explanation: A real motor driver cannot give more than its limit. A plant that goes on responding beyond it lets a controller be tuned against a machine that does not exist.

questions.question: A plant reports its position as it was before the step. Which rule catches it?
options: Consistency: over one step the position should move by the new velocity times the step
Determinism: two plants given the same commands should agree
Reset: position and velocity should be zero after a reset
Saturation: ten times the limit should do what the limit does
questions.explanation: After a step the position should have moved by the new velocity times the step. A plant that reports the old position is one step behind.

questions.question: A controller drives two plants to position 1 and both end at 1.0000. Why is that not enough?
options: The plant with no clamp got there at a peak speed of 22.71 against 14.70, past what the motor can do, and the end position is the one thing that is the same
It is enough: a controller is judged by where the plant ends
The two plants are the same class, so the test proves nothing
Both overshoot by the same amount, which the end position hides
questions.explanation: Both arrive. The unclamped plant did it 54 percent faster than the motor can go, and a test that looks only at the end sees no difference.

questions.question: What does passing the contract not tell you?
options: Whether the plant clamps its command
Whether two plants given the same commands agree
That the plant is the machine it stands for: a motor with the wrong time constant keeps every rule
Whether a reset returns it to rest
questions.explanation: The six rules check that the plant behaves like a plant. They cannot check that its gain and time constant are those of the real motor.
